rules.rule: A message-only exchange creates no task: only a reply to the message answers it.
A context holds many tasks; each reaches its own terminal state, and completing one leaves the others and the conversation open.

An initial request allocates its context and conversation atomically: sixteen concurrent deliveries leave one conversation, one message and one task, and fifteen duplicates; a crash around the unit leaves all of it or none.
A retry of an accepted message with a fresh context recovers the first context, conversation, message and task, and records nothing twice, also after a crash that lost the answer.
A context and task mismatch, a task the caller does not own and a terminal task are rejected, and write nothing.
A blocking wait that runs out is the documented deadline error; a task that failed or was canceled during the wait is answered as a task.
A task opened and completed after the waiting side is gone stays inspectable with its events; nothing is canceled.
A cancel request is recorded and answered with the task as it is; only the host reports canceled, which clears the request.
A status change without content records no message; status content records exactly one message of origin task_status, and bots see it only when they opt in to message.created.
Only protocol version 1.0 is served; streaming, push notifications and the extended card are rejected.

The two roles stay separate: the adapter reaches the engine through public packages only, its sink can neither open nor update a task, and nothing an agent writes changes who wrote it or acts as a command.
